newsitem.title: FRANCE: FRENCH ELECTION - Key constituencies - Latest.
newsitem.headline: FRENCH ELECTION - Key constituencies - Latest.

text.p: Results of Sunday's final round of the parliamentary election in key constituencies.
-- Former Socialist minister SEGOLENE ROYAL re-elected in Deux-Sevres constituency with 61.81 percent of the vote against 38.18 percent for Moreau Leopold of the centrist UDF.
-- PIERRE MOSCOVICI, co-author of the Socialist economic manifesto, wins in Doubs with 58.15 percent, to 41.85 percent for the outgoing RPR deputy Jean Geney.
-- Greens party spokeswoman DOMINIQUE VOYNET gains seat in Dole, eastern France, with 55.95 percent of the votes, beating UDF incumbent Gilbert Barbier (44.05 percent).
-- Free-marketeering former finance minister ALAIN MADELIN (UDF) re-elected in Ille-et-Vilaine with 55.14 percent, beating Socialist candidate Simone Bourges (44.85 percent).

-- Leftist former defence minister JEAN-PIERRE CHEVENEMENT re-elected in Belfort with 55.3 percent, in a three-way run-off against Jacques Bichet of the centrist UDF (26.03 percent) and National Front candidate Michel Algrin (18.65 percent).
-- Former Socialist minister SEGOLENE ROYAL re-elected in Deux-Sevres constituency with 61.81 percent of the vote against 38.18 percent for Moreau Leopold of the centrist UDF.
